_doc: What a UX sweep walks. Each journey is a goal a person has, not a click path: the persona finds the path. `personas` are ids from personas.json; `viewports` are desktop (1440x900) and/or phone (390x844). Start is a path on the fixture serve (seed.sh).

journeys.goal: Open bough for the first time today and work out what needs you, what is running and what changed since yesterday.
A session is waiting on a question for you. Find it, read the question with enough context to answer, answer it and see the agent continue.
Start a new session in the acme-todo repo asking it to add a 'due today' filter, and follow it until it finishes.
Pick a finished session that edited files. Review exactly what it changed, file by file, and decide whether you would keep it.
Open the pingd session that added flags and ask a follow-up that builds on its last answer; check the reply uses the earlier context.
Sessions say tests failed. Find out which tests, why, and get one of them fixed.
Start a long task, then change your mind mid-run: stop it or redirect it, and confirm nothing kept running.
Find every background job and background agent that is running or finished, see its output, and stop one.
Create a project for the handbook repo, file two existing sessions into it and start a thread there.
Open the Acme web app project and understand its state: main thread, other threads, what each is doing.
Find the session from over a week ago about colliding ids, and what the fix was, without scrolling through everything.
Tidy the list: archive what is done, bring one archived session back, and mark things seen.
Switch one session to a different model and effort for its next turn and confirm the change applied only there.
Do three things with the keyboard only via the command palette: new session, jump to a session, open Hooks.
Understand which hooks run, try one against a sample input and turn one off.
Use the Me page to decide what to work on this morning.
Look up what bough knows about a topic and check where a claim came from.
For one session, find out what context the agent had: instructions files, skills, tools, and how full the window is.
Give a session a screenshot or file and ask about it.
On a phone between meetings: see what finished, answer anything waiting, and send one short follow-up.
Ask for a file to be written in the scratch folder (not a git repo) and understand what happened and what to do instead.
Complete start-task and answer-ask with a screen reader's view of the page (accessibility tree only) and keyboard only.
